placement.rationale: Mid-cap placement balances the complete source-sized fractions beside letters and mixed-height figures. Top alignment lowers the denominators more heavily; bottom alignment raises the numerators and reaches beyond the existing Windows ascent. Center placement fits the existing metrics and retains all source differences.
placement.historical_limit: The charts do not establish a co-set historical text baseline. Row center 350 and 35-unit sidebearings are explicit modern layout choices. Full source physical dimensions and between-form differences remain.
placement.source_gap: Seek matching 12pt fractions or symbols co-set with letters or ordinary figures to establish historical baseline placement.

row_review.note: Fits use only fractions; shorter cent and percent retain native positions under the same row transform. The New York second row has only two fractions, so its zero residual is not an independent precision estimate. Five overlaid native rows were reviewed.

regular-fraction-12-atf-handy-1897-0.method: Estimate row skew from whole-form ink-box centers at threshold 150. Every row fit excludes the shorter cent/percent. All available traced fractions determine the row fit; their exact IDs and count are recorded. Use one row translation, preserving differences between forms. This is not a measured text baseline.

atf-handy-1897.method: Independent common-capital and repeated-footer physical scale.

atf-new-york-1897.method: Reviewed whole-form width/height fit to matching Handy fractions and symbols; one isotropic scale per source.

atf-handy-byu-1897.method: Reviewed whole-form width/height fit to matching Handy fractions and symbols; one isotropic scale per source.

atf-american-line-1906.method: Reviewed whole-form width/height fit to matching Handy fractions and symbols; one isotropic scale per source.

atf-desk-1898.method: Reviewed whole-form width/height fit to matching Handy fractions and symbols; one isotropic scale per source.

common_capital_fit.method: One isotropic least-squares fit to common capitals after measured row rotation; independent repeated footer transfers scale to fraction chart. Wider10/12pt S forms remain comparison-only and do not set scale.

footer_scale_transfer.method: Map 26 footer projection groups using threshold 170, combining the overlapping R/S pair in FOUNDERS. Measure ink bounds independently at five thresholds. Fit one isotropic 2D similarity transform to matched group centers. No fraction dimensions enter the fit.

quality_decisions: All 210 threshold trials across 42 whole impressions reviewed on fifteen PDF pages, alongside 55 native cells from six books.
NY150 supplies clear whole quarters, half and one-third; Handy three-quarters joins the slash to the denominator.

LOC170 two-thirds retains the complete numerator and denominator with both slash segments separate. NY, BYU and American usable thresholds introduce an upper slash/3-hook bridge; lower thresholds lose numerator ink. The independent intact impression supports the separated construction at this point size.
American150 one-eighth retains both counters and a separate slash. NY130 is intact but thinner; BYU has a persistent join.
BYU130 three-eighths and BYU150 five-eighths preserve complete four-part forms and both counters at higher native resolution; higher thresholds bridge the intended gaps.

American130 seven-eighths retains four complete parts and two counters; American150 joins both slash ends to the figures. LOC170 independently confirms the separate construction; NY and BYU join the lower slash at otherwise usable thresholds. Small native edge variation is retained.
BYU150 cent retains its complete stroke and counter; NY150 percent retains its upper connector and all three counters without the tiny pinholes seen in lower-threshold BYU traces.
One isotropic physical scale per book comes from independently matched common forms; no individual glyph height normalization. No parts assembled, holes filled or missing ink drawn.
identity_limit: Matched construction and proportional dimensions support grouping; identical historical punches or matrices are not established.
